title: Talent Symphony: Role Design and Onboarding Ops
author: Evelyn Park
content:
Overview:

Purpose: This playbook codifies how Redwood designs role definitions, runs equitable hiring and promotion processes, and executes fast, consistent onboarding using the internal toolchain. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, recruiting, and engineering managers.

Scope: policy and operational guidance that covers role design principles, multi-path career ladders, promotion rubrics, time-to-hire and onboarding SLAs, benefit alignment with role design, and the tooling and runbooks used for provisioning and measurement.

Principles (short):
- Outcome-first: roles focus on measurable outcomes and customer impact, not only tasks.
- Multipath mobility: career development recognizes technical, people-manager, and specialist paths.
- Equity and transparency: role expectations, rubrics, and processes are documented and visible to candidates and contributors.
- Fast handoffs: hiring and onboarding are designed to minimize time-to-impact while preserving quality.

1) Role design framework

A concise template every role must include (use this header in job descriptions):
- Role summary (1–2 sentences).
- Level and typical span (IC1–IC6, Mgr1–Mgr4).
- Key outcomes (3-5 measurable outcomes with KPIs).
- Core responsibilities (3–6 bullets).
- Cross-team dependencies and stakeholders.
- Required and preferred qualifications (skill emphasis, not gatekeeping).
- Typical career trajectories and possible lateral moves.

Example: Senior Software Engineer (IC4) — Key outcomes: 1) Reduce inference cost per token by 12% quarter-over-quarter, 2) Lead one cross-team rollout, 3) Mentor two engineers to promotion.

Level rubric (summary table, textual):
- Level: IC3 | Scope: owns a feature or subsystem | Impact: improves subsystem reliability or performance | Expected outcomes: shipping well-scoped projects, mentoring juniors.
- Level: IC4 | Scope: owns features across subsystems | Impact: sustained performance improvements, influence across teams | Expected outcomes: lead projects with cross-team rollouts.
- Level: IC5+ | Scope: organization-level initiatives | Impact: sets technical direction, large owner of cross-cutting systems | Expected outcomes: define strategy, drive execution at scale.

Promotion rubric (core signals to evaluate):
1. Delivery: consistent delivery against outcomes for 6–12 months.
2. Scope expansion: ownership beyond immediate team boundaries.
3. Impact: measurable business/technical metrics improved.
4. Leadership: peer influence, mentorship, and decision-making maturity.
5. Judgment: quality trade-offs and ability to operate with ambiguous inputs.

Process: manager initiates packet -> calibration with peer manager -> people-ops review for equity checks -> live panel (2 peers + skip-level) -> outcome recorded in HR system. Timing expectation: packet to outcome within 6 weeks.

2) Hiring and time-to-fill targets

Standard stages and owner responsibilities:
1. Requisition (Hiring manager + People Ops): publish JD using role template and level rubric.
2. Sourcing (Recruiter): build candidate slate; target 6–8 screened candidates within 10 business days for high-priority product/infra roles.
3. Screening (Hiring manager + recruiter): initial technical screen within 3 business days of application.
4. Loop (Interview panel): structured rubric-based interviews, complete loop within 7 calendar days of first technical screen.
5. Offer (Comp & People Ops): approval and offer within 3 business days of final decision.

Target KPIs (operational):
- Time-to-offer (median): 35 calendar days for standard roles, 25 for critical hires.
- Offer acceptance rate goal: >= 75%.
- Diversity slate requirement: at least 30% underrepresented candidates in final 6 screened slate for mid-senior roles.

Interview guidance and scoring: use the level rubric and three buckets for each interview (Skills, Problem Solving, Collaboration) with a 1–5 score. Interviewers must record concrete evidence for each score (no free-text-only judgments).

3) Onboarding and time-to-impact SLAs

Onboarding objectives: safety, productivity, network integration. Measured SLAs and metrics:
- Badge & account provisioning: 48 hours after start date (50% target; escalations if >72 hours).
- Dev environment ready: within 3 business days.
- First-ticket onboarding task assigned: day 1.
- MVP contribution (first merged PR or runbook update): within 14 calendar days.
- Fully ramped contributor (meeting role-level outcomes independently): 90 days (expected).

Onboarding stages and checklist (mandatory steps):
1. Pre-boarding (People Ops + Hiring manager): welcome email, first-week agenda, required training links, hardware shipping confirmation.
2. Day 0–1: provisioning, manager 1:1, buddy assignment, team intro.
3. Week 1: discovery rotations, runbook walkthroughs, small onboarding project.
4. Month 1: performance syncs, feedback session, training completion.
5. Month 3: formal ramp review and development plan.

Automated checks (internal tools): the onboarding dashboard (OnboardOps) reports provisioning progress and open blocker tickets. People Ops will automatically contact the escalation channel #onboarding-escalations if any mandatory item is >72 hours overdue.

4) Benefits and perks alignment with role design

Redwood philosophy: benefits support sustainable contributor performance and mobility. Highlights relevant to role design and hiring conversations:
- Flexible work stipend: home office and internet allowance up to $1,100/year prorated.
- Care leave & parental policy: 18 weeks primary, 12 weeks non-primary, phased return coaching.
- Sabbatical eligibility: after 5 years of continuous service, 4–8 week paid sabbatical option.
- Learning & mobility fund: $2,000/year per employee for role transitions, certifications, or conference attendance.
- Mental health and wellbeing: expanded EAP, 10 therapy sessions/year fully covered, quarterly wellness stipend.

Recruiters must be prepared to discuss benefits at offer stage and to match role-level expectations (e.g., market adjustment for senior ICs or managers).

5) Internal tools & provisioning runbooks (how-to)

Primary tools and owners:
- OnboardOps (People Ops): manages pre-boarding checklist, provisioning, and dashboards.
- Identity (IAM): access control, SSO groups, and role-based permission templates (owner: Security).
- Tooling catalog (Service Catalog): lists provisioning steps for databases, clusters, and SaaS tools.
- Learning LMS: course assignments and tracking for role-specific curricula.

Sample provisioning commands and quick runbook notes (for engineers managing access):
- Create service ticket in Service Catalog: `sc create --type provisioning --user <email> --role <role-template>`
- Grant temporary dev cluster access (48h): `iam grant --user <email> --resource dev-cluster --expiry 48h`
- Reprovision workstation (hardware replacement): open OnboardOps ticket with label `hardware-reprovision` and attach order ID.

Access review cadence: owners must validate IAM groups quarterly; people-ops will surface anomalies and deprovision stale accounts after 45 days of inactivity following notification.

6) Operating rhythms, ownership, and escalation

Rituals and responsibilities:
- People Ops weekly hiring sync: review open reqs, blockers, and pipeline health (owner: Head of Talent).
- Manager calibration sessions: monthly cross-org calibration to reduce leveling drift (owner: Org Leads + People Ops).
- Onboarding retrospectives: quarterly review of onboarding SLAs and feedback (owner: People Ops + sample of recent hires).

Escalation path (when SLAs break):
1. Escalate to People Ops partner and hiring manager.
2. If unresolved in 48 hours, escalate to Head of Talent.
3. Critical security or access issues: immediately alert Security on-call and tag #security-ops.

7) Measurement and continuous improvement

Core metrics tracked monthly: time-to-offer median, offer acceptance rate, onboarding time-to-MVP, first-90-day retention, hiring source conversion rates, and diversity slate compliance. People Ops publishes a monthly talent dashboard and a quarterly deep-dive with recommendations.

Improvement loop: collect feedback at day 7, day 30, and day 90 from new hires and managers; incorporate findings into a rolling backlog.

Appendices (templates and sample text)

A. Job description header (copyable):
- Title: [Role] — Level [IC#/Mgr#]
- One-line summary: [impact-focused sentence]
- Outcomes (3): [Outcome 1, KPI], [Outcome 2, KPI], [Outcome 3, KPI]
- Responsibilities: bullet list
- Qualifications: required/preferred
- Career trajectories: two example next roles

B. Sample onboarding 14-day plan (text):
- Day 0: Accounts + buddy intro + hardware check.
- Day 1: Team kickoff + first-ticket assignment.
- Days 2–5: System walkthroughs + small project.
- Week 2: Cross-team intro + first PR.

C. Promotion packet checklist (text):
- Manager summary + evidence mapping to rubric, peer feedback, impact metrics, learning & development notes, and recommended next level.
